chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from him, peace be upon him, that he said:

Regarding a man who says, "If I die, then my slave is free," while the man has a debt, he said: "If he dies while he has a debt that has encompassed the price of the slave, the slave is sold. And if it has not encompassed the price of the slave, the slave is made to work toward repaying the debt of his master, and he is free by it when he has fully paid it."

key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: he is made to work or earn toward payment
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave whose emancipation was made conditional upon the master's death
key_terms.بِثَمَنِ: by the price or market value, used here for assessing whether debt covers the slave's value
key_terms.حُرٌّ: free; the state of emancipation from bondage
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt owed by the deceased, which has legal priority in estate settlement
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: repayment or discharge of an obligation, here the master's debt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says his slave will be free after his death while he still owes debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave's posthumous emancipation when the deceased master leaves unpaid debt. The debt takes precedence over the emancipation bequest to the extent of the slave's value; if the full value is not covered by the debt, the slave works to settle the remaining debt and then becomes free.
